fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Fenced Sections
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions of travel on the street.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges to maintain clear vehicle-width clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders arriving under low-visibility conditions can locate it without delay.
• Clear a path along the exterior perimeter fence line so responders can move on foot between the front and rear of the property.
• Install a gate or latch on the rear fence section that can be opened quickly from the outside without tools or a key.
• Post the gate location on the exterior fence so responders can find rear access without walking the full perimeter.
• Keep the area directly in front of the driveway entrance free of parked vehicles so emergency vehicles can turn in without obstruction.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings without pushing through overgrowth.
• Maintain the walkway free of stored items, equipment, or overgrown plantings so it remains passable for responders on foot.
• Identify a flat, open staging area near the driveway where a second emergency vehicle can park without blocking the access point.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Vegetation Separation; Scattered Shrubs; Single Access Route; Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the house and any outbuildings.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open gaps between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants growing directly against the exterior walls of the house.
• Clear ground vegetation within the immediate area surrounding the structure.
• Separate scattered shrubs from nearby trees so plants are not touching or overlapping.
• Cut back scattered trees near the structure so their branches do not connect with shrubs or ground plants below them.
• Remove dead or dry ground vegetation throughout the property, particularly in areas close to the house.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along both sides.
• Maintain the driveway width wide enough for emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Thin vegetation on both sides of the access route to keep the path visible and open.
• Move any stored wood, debris, or flammable materials away from the exterior walls of the house.
• Create open ground between the scattered shrubs and the structure by removing plants in between.
